## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- This break has no listed tide preference to compare the sources with.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Fifteen sources from fourteen publishers; fourteen were read directly. Surfer Today returned 403 (Cloudflare) and is kept unchanged as web_search. No peer-reviewed source could be read. Crossref lists Schoonees, Lenhoff and Raw (1999), 'Preventing Natural Breaching of the Major Sand Spit Protecting the Port of Walvis Bay' (Coastal Engineering 1998, doi 10.1061/9780784404119.109), on the Pelican Point spit. It has no abstract in Crossref, and the ASCE page is behind Cloudflare, so nothing was recorded. WIND CONFLICT REMAINS. NE (45) comes from Surf-Forecast, MyWaveFinder and Desert Tracks. MyWaveFinder gives NE for every Namibian spot, and these three may all trace back to Surf-Forecast's templated value. E (90) comes from Surfer Today (unreadable), and SE-E, ideally SE (135), from Wave Safari. The profile's 100 lies between them. Surf Holidays' 'Wind: South, South-West' is the prevailing wind, not an offshore one. Swell direction: SW, or W-SW, everywhere. South Africa Surf Tours and Surf Holidays favour more west, and Desert Tracks says the big west swells that scour the bank have become less reliable. Period: nobody gives a number; all say a big long-period groundswell, with short-period swell not reaching the bay. Size: Surfer Today 4-8 ft and Yeeew 'up to 8 ft' are below the profile's 12 ft maximum. Yeeew is marked agrees false; Surfer Today's earlier agrees true was kept unchanged because the page cannot be read (rule 2); South Africa Surf Tours gives only a 3 m open-ocean chart threshold. TIDE (the profile has no value): low from Stab (2023) and Yeeew; all from Surf-Forecast, Surfer Today, Wave Safari, MyWaveFinder and Surf Holidays. 'All' is the better-supported value, with a lean to low tide. Seasonality: May-September agrees everywhere. BATHYMETRY RECENCY (sand bottom): dated sources say the bank keeps changing. The Inertia (2023) says the bank was tricky for days. South Africa Surf Tours (2025) says the sand shifts every off-season. Desert Tracks (2026) says the wave has degraded into sections, with about 1 million m3 of sand a year moving along the bay. Surf Holidays says the bank only formed after a late-1970s wind shift. Low-weight sources: Yeeew Mag (clear factual errors), Wave Safari (template fields contradict its own text) and MyWaveFinder (templated).

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 4 ft; scale: not stated [S3] · 3 m; converted: 9.8 ft; scale: swell charts (offshore) [S13] (/ m) | conflicting | S3, S13 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | big to huge long-period swell (no number) | documented | S4, S5, S11, S13, S15 | no separate setting; working range 4–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 8 ft (2.4 m) (scale not stated) | documented | S3, S7 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: Surfer Today (search summary) lists a size range starting at 4 feet without stating the scale, while South Africa Surf Tours says to ignore anything under 3 m on the charts (offshore swell, about 9.8 ft by 3 / 0.3048); the two cannot be reconciled without knowing Surfer Today's scale.
  - S3 (Surfer Today): “The listed swell direction is W/SW, with a size range of 4 to 8 feet.”
  - S13 (South Africa Surf Tours): “Don't consider anything smaller than 3 metres on the charts.”
- **Ideal range**: Surf Bugle says the perfect day comes from a huge long-period swell, Surf Europe and Desert Tracks a big or large long-period groundswell, South Africa Surf Tours really big SW to W swells and MyWaveFinder a powerful SW swell; no excerpt gives an ideal size in numbers.
  - S4 (Surf Bugle (Ben Mondy)): “A massive Atlantic low creates a huge long period swell. Short-period swells don't make it into the bay.”
  - S5 (Surf Europe): “needing a big long-period groundswell from the Roaring Forties to wrap in at just the right angle”
  - S13 (South Africa Surf Tours): “really big, SW to W (the more West the better) swells”
  - S11 (MyWaveFinder): “Skeleton Bay is a fickle and inconsistent surf spot that needs a powerful SW swell”
  - S15 (Desert Tracks): “only on a large long-period south-west groundswell”
- **Maximum suitable**: Surfer Today (search summary) lists a size range of 4 to 8 feet and Yeeew (a low-weight source with factual errors) says wave size can reach up to 8 ft / 2.4 m; neither states whether this is face or offshore swell height.
  - S3 (Surfer Today): “The listed swell direction is W/SW, with a size range of 4 to 8 feet.”
  - S7 (Yeeew!): “Wave size: Can reach up to 8 feet (2.4 meters)”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: Surfer Today (search summary) lists a size range starting at 4 feet without stating the scale, while South Africa Surf Tours says to ignore anything under 3 m on the charts (offshore swell, about 9.8 ft by 3 / 0.3048); the two cannot be reconciled without knowing Surfer Today's scale.
- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives southwest as the optimum angle and MyWaveFinder and Desert Tracks name a SW swell, while South Africa Surf Tours says SW to W with the more west the better.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast, MyWaveFinder (templated for all Namibian spots) and Desert Tracks give a north-easterly offshore, Surfer Today (search summary) lists east as offshore, and Wave Safari says SE to E, ideally SE.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast, Surfer Today (search summary), Wave Safari, MyWaveFinder and Surf Holidays say it works on all tides, while Yeeew and a visiting pro quoted by Stab (2023) say it is best or much better at low tide.
- **Seasonality · secondary season**: Surfer Today (search summary) says the waves break all year round and Surf Holidays gives 'All year', while South Africa Surf Tours says it only starts working in the southern winter months, so whether there is surf outside May to September is disputed.
